original_value: Privacy preserving data publishing has received considerable attention for publishing useful information while preserving data privacy. The existing privacy preserving data publishing methods for multiple sensitive attributes do not consider the situation that different values of a sensitive attribute may have different sensitivity requirements. To solve this problem, we defined three security levels for different sensitive attribute values that have different sensitivity requirements, and given an      L  s l      -diversity model for multiple sensitive attributes. Following this, we proposed three specific greed algorithms based on the maximal-bucket first (MBF), maximal single-dimension-capacity first (MSDCF) and maximal multi-dimension-capacity first (MMDCF) algorithms and the maximal security-level first (MSLF) greed policy, named as MBF based on MSLF (MBF-MSLF), MSDCF based on MSLF (MSDCF-MSLF) and MMDCF based on MSLF (MMDCF-MSLF), to implement the      L  s l      -diversity model for multiple sensitive attributes. The experimental results show that the three algorithms can greatly reduce the information loss of the published microdata, but their runtime is only a small increase, and their information loss tends to be stable with the increasing of data volume. And they can solve the problem that the information loss of MBF, MSDCF and MMDCF increases greatly with the increasing of sensitive attribute number.

result.paraphrase: Privacy-preserving data publishing has attracted extensive attention because it enables the release of useful information while protecting data privacy. However, existing methods for privacy-preserving publishing with multiple sensitive attributes do not account for the fact that different values of a sensitive attribute may require different sensitivity levels. To address this issue, we introduced three security levels for sensitive-attribute values with varying sensitivity requirements and proposed an Lsl-diversity model for multiple sensitive attributes. Based on the maximal-bucket first (MBF), maximal single-dimension-capacity first (MSDCF), and maximal multi-dimension-capacity first (MMDCF) algorithms, together with the maximal security-level first (MSLF) greedy policy, we further designed three greedy algorithms: MBF-MSLF, MSDCF-MSLF, and MMDCF-MSLF, to realize the Lsl-diversity model for multiple sensitive attributes. Experimental results indicate that these three algorithms can substantially reduce information loss in published microdata while increasing runtime only slightly, and their information loss remains stable as data volume grows. They also address the problem that information loss in MBF, MSDCF, and MMDCF rises sharply as the number of sensitive attributes increases.
